reviews.review_description:
City of Hunger: Survive throws you into fast-paced, 5-minute survival scenarios—whether it’s the streets or a house—where chaos reigns from the start. The introduction is gripping, dropping you into the action with no mercy, and the weapons feel satisfying, especially the axe for some brutal takedowns.
The game shines with quirky, unexpected moments, like a zombie bursting from a belly (a clear Alien nod) then battling it on top of the host himself. With more sets on the way, this early-access gem is fun, varied, and well-executed, making it worth keeping an eye on. If you love short, intense survival challenges, this is a solid pick! 🔥

developer_response.body: Thanks so much, metaquesta99! 🙏 Glad the axe feels satisfying — it was the first weapon we tuned. Love that you caught the Alien nod, more quirky moments like that are coming in the next sets. Appreciate you jumping in early, it means a lot for a solo dev. See you in the streets!

reviews.review_description:
As a display of graphics rendering techniques it's very impressive, but as a game it's terrible.

You move at a snail's pace. It's like walking through quicksand. Maybe there's a run button but I haven't found it yet. There's no tutorial.

Grabbing objects is hit or miss.

Weapons wobble around making aiming very difficult. Two handed weapons wobble like crazy.  The tracking is the worst I've ever encountered in my decade of playing VR games.

The first area gets old in a hurry. Walking through quicksand in a confined section of a street while hoards of zombies attack from all sides is no fun when aiming is so ridiculously difficult because of the wonky weapon handling.

It was a relief when I finally reached the Game Over screen. I would like to see the other levels but it's just too miserable to continue playing at this point.

The rendering techniques are the only aspect of this game that are enjoyable.  Fire, smoke, lighting effects, are all very impressive.  But the graphics are inconsistent and very overdone.

At times the visual effects are layered on so thick that the scene turns into a confusing blurry mess.

I do recommend taking a look at it, but know what you're getting.

For me it's worth the $2 as a graphics demo and a donation to the developer. I hope they can get the gameplay sorted out because this could be pretty awesome.

developer_response.body: Thanks for the detailed feedback, Jioxx — and glad you liked the visuals. We've noted everything down and we're investigating the weapon tracking issues to replicate them here and improve in future updates. Your experience really helps, and we appreciate the support.

reviews.review_description:
I love indie games but this is just a demo. 

No accurate hit collision, you move slow, takes the same amount of hits as it does to shoot to down a zombie, reloading is a chore, limited ammo.  Hitting a zombie anywhere on its body cause the same damage.      

Want to survive 5 minutes just move around really slow. 

Games does look good though but it’s way to dark.

developer_response.body:
I'm sorry, but I think you're talking about the wrong game. For starters, this isn't a demo. The game features 5 levels—currently on sale for $1—each with a different setting and set of challenges. In fact, there is another game *inside* the game, and a lot of people will understand what I mean by that.

As for the difficulty of reloading, you just grab the magazine and move it toward the gun, just like in most games. It's actually very straightforward because the gameplay is more arcade-oriented.

Regarding the bullet collision, you're mistaken. Shooting an enemy in the leg does not do the same damage as shooting them in the head. On the contrary, they react differently depending on which body part is hit, with different animations for each. However, these are not indestructible zombies that only die from headshots—they are people infected by a parasite, so they can be killed with just a few shots to the body. I don't see why that would be a problem.

And I appreciate your comment about the graphics. I'm glad you found something positive to say, considering it's the CHEAPEST AND BEST-LOOKING game on the Meta Quest 3. But if you think it's too dark, you can use the flashlight attached to your head—I don't think you noticed it.

reviews.review_description: I bought this game with no video and no information, but for $1.99, I figured I can't turn it down.  VERY, VERY INTENSE.  This is what a zombie game should be. There are no instructions, no cheats, no help you have to SURVIVE. Nonstop zombie horde. Very dark but has great looking zombies when compared to so many other shooters.  It still has work to be done, but for the price it is, and the excitement and thrill of playing it now, it is worth a lot more than $1.99.  Changes I would suggest:  add a setting to control music, gun and zombie volumes.  It was very dark so maybe add a setting to lighten it up a little more instead of using the Quest controls to do this. Parts were a little blurry, like the titles as you dropped from the helicopter. Maybe have a walkie talkie with a connection to the helicopter you were on that the person above is looking for you and helps you know where to go next. A light direction/hint and tip every now and then when stuck or lost. You have some great looking zombies, maybe add a few more that are different, so we are not shooting the exact same ones over and over.  Change of hair color/clothing/shoes etc...  I can't wait to see what comes next. After posting this I watched a video on YouTube where that player had a blue arrow showing them where to go. My game did not have that.  But I did notice that their blue arrows didn't show up until sometime after the timer ran down to zero and they were out or close to being out of bullets.

developer_response.body:
Jeff, thank you for taking a chance on us with no video — that means a lot. Glad it felt INTENSE, that's exactly the vibe.

Great notes: a brightness slider, separate volumes for music/guns/zombies, and a light direction hint are all on our short list. The blurry intro titles and the blue arrow timing are bugs i  fixing — the arrow should show earlier, not after you’re out of ammo.

More zombie variety (hair, clothes) is coming with the next sets too. Thanks for the detailed feedback, it helps a solo dev a ton. See you in the city!

reviews.review_description: Honestly it’s got a few flaws but I am having fun with it. Few updates though please devs. Dig the play style and levels. You have to have good aim and think ahead always.  Keep up the great work.
Hello to the developers: the game suffers from significant slowdowns and a lack of sharpness; it really needs an update. It isn't really playable on the Quest 3.

developer_response.body:
Thank you for your feedback, and I'm sorry to hear about your experience.

In some cases, the Quest can experience an issue where the first launch after installation or an update may result in lower performance than expected. If you completely close the game and launch it again, this often resolves the problem.

If the issue persists after restarting the game, please let me know which areas were affected so I can investigate further and continue improving the experience.

reviews.review_description:
Great graphics, but it's a little overkill at times with the amount of clutter on screen, like exploding heads making visibility somewhat frustrating. I also had an issue with blinding white light and reflections during the first street scene. I'm not sure if this is intentional, but it sure made me glad I don't suffer from photosensitivity... 
I must agree with other reviewers regarding aiming. At times it feels smooth; a headshot from distance feels good, but when you're standing point blank unloading into their face and nothing hits, it kinda breaks the immersion! 
My only other quibble was the lack of smooth turning and the speed at which you move. I get that zombies are known for their slow pace, but surely we can still sprint? 

With that out of the way, here's what I enjoyed about this game: 

Being dropped straight into the action with no hand holding. 
The immersion is there; the game just needs a polish. 
99p in the sale is all I paid for this game, and the regular price is only £1.99. Plus, it looks like the devs are actively paying attention and replying to reviews, which gives me hope that any issues I had may well get patched in an update. 

It's not a triple A title, but guys neither is the price! I have no regrets with the purchase and am hopeful for an update once the devs have gathered their feedback!

reviews.review_title: I was sweating the while time!
reviews.review_description: Only $1.99? I can't believe it! The graphics are giving me Arizona Sunshine and Resident Evil vibes. This is probably the only zombie VR game that's actually scared me—I was sweating the whole time! This is what a real survival game feels like. So intense!

developer_response.body:
Thank you so much! Reviews like yours make all the hard work worth it.

I'm really happy to hear the atmosphere reminded you of Arizona Sunshine and Resident Evil—that's a huge compliment. My goal was to create a survival horror experience where every bullet counts and the tension never lets up.

I hope you enjoy discovering everything the game has to offer. Thanks again for your support, and have fun surviving! 🧟🔦
